# Trade in Minutes! Rationality-Driven Agentic System for Quantitative Financial Trading

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Building a rationality-driven multi-agent LLM system that develops and optimizes programmatic trading bots offline and deploys them for minute-level quantitative trading in stock index futures and crypto markets. | “we present TiMi (Trade in Minutes), a rationality-driven multi-agent system that architecturally decouples strategy development from minute-level deployment.” |
| **architecture** | Four agents: macro analysis agent (strategies from technical indicators), strategy adaptation agent (pair-specific rules/parameters), bot evolution agent (writes layered code bots), feedback reflection agent (linear-programming parameter solving); policy, optimization, deployment stages; CPU-only bot deployment. | “(1) policy stage — complex reasoning and strategy development occur in an offline environment, fully leveraging the capabilities of specialized agents, including actions of \mathcal{A}_{\text{ma}} , \mathcal{A}_{\text{sa}} , and \mathcal{A}_{\text{be}} to generate prototype trading bots” |
| **data** | Market technical indicators (volume, amplitude, K-lines, funding rates) for 213 trading pairs in U.S. stock index futures (CME) and mainstream/altcoin crypto futures (Binance), minute-level frequency. | “We select top-tier exchanges with high liquidity, i.e., CME for stock index futures and Binance for cryptocurrencies.” |
| **window** | Backtesting on 2024 historical data; live trading from January to April 2025. Progressive validation: historical development, real-time simulation, then live trading. | “Table 3: Live trading comparison of mainstream methods across U.S. stock index futures and cryptocurrency markets from 2025 January to April.” |
| **models** | DeepSeek-V3 for semantic analysis, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct for code programming, DeepSeek-R1 for mathematical reasoning. | “We strategically adopt DeepSeek-V3 for semantic analysis, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct for code programming, and DeepSeek-R1 for mathematical reasoning.” |
| **baselines** | Quantitative: MACD, momentum, grid, pairs trading, ETF&PCA, TSMOM, OFI; ML&RL: LSTM, Autoformer, PatchTST, DQN, DDPG; LLM agents: FinGPT, FinMem, TradingAgents. | “Baselines. We compare TiMi against three representative categories: (1) quantitative methods, including MACD (Wang & Kim, 2018) optimized by historical volatility, momentum strategy (Jegadeesh & Titman, 1993), grid trading (Griffin et al., 2003)” |
| **headline_result** | Live trading (Jan–Apr 2025): ARR 6.4%, 8.0%, 13.7% on U.S. stock index futures, mainstream coins, altcoins; SR 0.74, 0.79, 0.86; MDD 20.3%, 25.1%, 32.8%; 213 pairs. | “\| TiMi (ours) \| 6.4 \| 0.74 \| 20.3 \| 8.0 \| 0.79 \| 25.1 \| 13.7 \| 0.86 \| 32.8 \| 213 \| minute” |
| **costs** | Models order fees and periodic funding rates; LIMIT orders for entry to get maker fees and avoid entry slippage; funding-rate-based order reduction; pre-trade price deviation check. Deployment end-to-end latency avg 137 ms. | “We model and mitigate two primary costs: order fees and periodic funding rates. TiMi employs LIMIT orders for entry to capture favorable maker fees and eliminate entry slippage.” |
| **uncertainty** | Cross-pair return dispersion reported (σ = 11.03% for TiMi vs 29.64% for DDPG); latency std dev and P99. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported. | “TiMi exhibits markedly performance stability with reduced variance ( \sigma = 11.03%) and rare tail events ( < 2%), indicating more consistent returns over market dynamics compared to alternatives.” |
| **leakage_controls** | Live trading evaluation in 2025 after development on historical data; authors note LLM-agent baselines may exploit posterior information in backtests. No explicit contamination control described. | “We implement a progressive validation: initial strategy development using historical data, followed by trading simulation with real-time market data, and culminating in live trading evaluation.” |
| **limitations** | Need for an optimization stage limits zero-shot performance when porting to new markets; broader concerns about market dynamics, liquidity, fairness and institutional-retail gap. | “The necessity of the optimization stage limits the zero-shot performance of trading bots developed by TiMi when porting to new markets.” |
| **release** | Authors promise to open-source deployment implementation and release corner case list; no location given. | “Crucially, we will open-source the implementation of TiMi product for deployment and release the key corner case list (from both back simulation and live deployment).” |
